50 Ways to Leave Another: creative and commercial treatment

Working limited-series concept · Owner-supplied premise with development proposals · Review draft, November 9, 2026
Independent development proposal — no studio, platform, artist or label affiliation implied.
Independent professional review: PENDING. Not legal advice, clearance, a commission, an offer or a representation agreement.

Pitch site · Concise producer pitch · Rights checklist · Sources

The hook

A professional contract killer discovers that her lover has betrayed her with someone they both trusted. He knows exactly what she is capable of. Everyone expects revenge. Her most consequential choice is to refuse both retaliation and the assignment—and leave.

Core question: What happens when a person whose livelihood depends on control decides to stop allowing others to determine her choices?

Format and audience — proposal: a premium serialized thriller conceived as a limited series for adult audiences interested in psychological tension, intimate betrayal, agency and music-led storytelling. This is a positioning proposal, not evidence of audience demand, buyer interest, financing or a finalized episode order.

Creative authority and continuity

The current owner-supplied foundation establishes the profession, betrayal by a lover and shared trusted person, expected revenge, and eventual refusal of retaliation and the assignment. These are fictional narrative facts, not claims about real people.

Existing project materials explore a five-song EP and five-part music/story progression, the return of a title song in different production states and a studio as dramatic space. Those remain development references. They do not finalize this thriller's episode count, runtime, names, biographies, setting, secondary plots, on-screen collaborators or soundtrack obligations. No new finalized scripts or character biographies are invented here.

The story: reclaiming the decision

Foundation: the protagonist earns her living through control. Her lover knowingly risks a relationship with someone accustomed to decisive action. Betrayal makes revenge the anticipated response; the trusted third person's role makes the breach intimate rather than abstract.

Proposed dramatic movement: discovery makes a familiar solution available. As she tests what action would actually reclaim her life, retaliation begins to resemble another task organized around other people's choices. Refusing the assignment alongside the relationship makes the ending an active withdrawal of consent. The suspense comes from whether she can stop performing the role that everyone—including herself—expects.

Open development questions: what the assignment is, how it intersects with the relationship, who knows about the betrayal, which consequences follow refusal, and how the final departure is dramatized. These need the owner's acceptance and writers' work. The story must earn independence through choices, not suggest that violence is a universal response to betrayal. No diagnosis or real-life analogue is assigned to any character.

Autonomy, identity, the economics of intimacy and the difference between power and freedom provide the thematic frame. Psychological tension and consequence are the promise; specific action sequences, locations and production scale remain undecided.

Music as narrative

Creator account: an existing human-recorded song and its development helped reactivate the fictional storyline. The private source archive is not reproduced here. The public project also documents a Suno-assisted demo/interpretation; its exact version, inputs and applicable plan/workflow remain to be verified.

Proposal: allow one musical idea to change meaning as the protagonist changes her relationship to control. A sparse opening, an interrupted motif or a fuller later performance could distinguish anticipation from a choice actually lived. These are development options, not instructions to reproduce Paul Simon's recording or a named artist's style, voice or music.

The existing five-part map offers a useful working method: early version, inventory, fracture, witnessing, presence. A writers' room and music lead should test that progression against the current thriller foundation instead of treating five tracks as five mandatory episodes. Each composition, performance, arrangement, render and editorial cue needs its own version and permission record.

A potential original soundtrack could create music-first storytelling, featured recordings and separate screen/music releases. Sync opportunities are contingent on the buyer's specifications, authorized chain of title, actual versions and negotiated scope. The concept is not a cleared catalog submission. No music is included in this treatment or pitch PDF.

Potential Music & Screen Partnership — UMG / Drake Concept

This is an unsolicited hypothesis, not an approach made to an artist or an accepted relationship. Drake illustrates an established-artist role; another suitable artist or an independent team could fill it. No need for a “comeback,” reputational injury, motive or desire to participate is asserted.

Creative value to explore: a coherent narrative and music-development process could give an artist room to contribute original work to a screen property, with clear credit, approvals and fair licensing rather than a request to reproduce an existing hit. Audience re-engagement is a possible objective to research, not a promised result.

Potential contribution What would need agreement
Artist: original soundtrack writing/performance or a commissioned featured recording Scope, creative authority, schedule, fee, human contributions, composition/master interests, delivery and promotional approvals
Artist: executive production or artist-owned narrative contributions A substantive defined role, underlying rights, retained ownership/licensing, credit, approval boundaries and any compensation; no title merely presumed
Label/publisher/production entity: music supervision, production, clearance, soundtrack promotion and coordinated releases Identify each authorized entity; define responsibilities, costs, licenses, exclusivity, accounting, distribution, recoupment and approvals
Loptr Lab: originating premise, project direction, existing development record and collaboration framework Verify private authorship/title records, reserved rights, writing/production scope, fair compensation, accessible process and publication permissions

No budget, royalty split, projection, financing, distribution or artist commitment is manufactured. Business, creative and clearance responsibilities would be allocated in a negotiated agreement. No one is authorized to incur expenses on another party's behalf.

Official-source context, checked November 9, 2026: Republic's current About page identifies it as a UMG division, associates OVO with Drake and Young Money with Lil Wayne, and describes Federal Films as its film/TV division. UMG's dated February 7, 2025 announcement includes Federal Films in Republic Collective growth initiatives. UMG's Polygram page separately describes a music-driven film/TV arm. OVO Sound's own site describes its founders. These public descriptions justify researching possible roles; they do not identify the entity able to approve a particular artist performance, composition, master or screen deal.

Historical UMG material lists earlier Drake/Cash Money relationships. It is not evidence of today's contract. The Young Money URL redirected to Lil Wayne's store, not a current artist-contract register. Current signatories, OVO/Young Money contractual relationships, submission policies and authority over any desired recording remain unresolved. See the source register for exact URLs, dates and limits.

If a proposed partner declines: preserve the originating concept, honor any existing rights, stop implying that partner's involvement and continue development with another appropriately scoped artist/team or independent original music. No named artist is a narrative dependency.

The production history is a collaboration laboratory

PRODUCTION-001 treats the owner's account as a chance to clarify roles and correct misunderstandings. The reported November 7, 2024 engineering-stage resampling decision is distinct from the creator's brief and her account that she did not request it. Original correspondence, agreements and sessions were not inspected for this draft; claims remain attributed.

The reported approximately $618.30 in likely studio payments, human recording, mix, Suno interpretation and later delivery questions are different evidence categories. They establish neither damages nor wrongdoing nor commercial readiness. The engineer's full responses and qualifying evidence must remain in the private review record. A quality disagreement and a clearance question require different tests.

The desired outcome is a better process: versioned briefs; accepted roles/capabilities; approval before material source changes; sample disclosures; clear session/stem delivery; response and correction opportunities; accurate credits and compensation; and accessible, affordable choices. A creator's access needs or limited budget should prompt clearer scope and support, not assumptions about ability or disclosure of personal financial/health information.

Professional invitation and next decision

Producers and writers can test the story foundation; a music supervisor can define version and cue needs; engineers/producers can scope a cleared recording path; publishers/labels/artist representatives can verify authority and appropriate routes; counsel can review title, samples, sync, privacy, trademarks and agreements. No professional is engaged by this document.

Before circulating protected music or soliciting a transaction, complete the rights-and-clearance checklist and review actual evidence privately. Netflix's official policy requires an appropriate intermediary with an existing Netflix relationship and rejects unsolicited materials; this public site does not provide direct access or guarantee consideration. Other companies' policies require separate verification.

Owner decisions for this draft: confirm public premise/positioning; identify which older continuity remains a proposal; approve visual treatment; authorize the exact sanitized history/cost language after any needed source/participant review; choose the next professional development task and permitted outreach scope. No main merge, partner contact, rights-dependent music use or production commitment is authorized by a green build.
